reasons: Tests in frontend/src/lib/format.test.ts cover resolve, the dangling path and every tier label.
Tests in frontend/src/render.test.tsx check that every citation in the records resolves.
I did not run these tests in this review.

terms.meaning: the set of source items given to one case
a claim that cites an id that is not in any pack
a number from 1 to 4 showing how authoritative a source is, from final standard down to hearsay
a fixed reference case used to test the system

depends_on: packages/schema/case_input.py (named as the source of the tier labels)
used_by: frontend/src/views/Portfolio.tsx (passes the index to the page, per the render test)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose note and imports
sections.what: The header explains that a missing source is shown rather than skipped, and brings in the artifact types.

sections.name: EvidenceIndex
sections.title: The lookup shape
sections.what: Holds two maps: one from evidence id to item, and one from case to its evidence pack.
sections.why: Two maps let a page find one item quickly and also list every item in a case.
sections.watch_out: Both maps are built together. Keep them in step if either is changed.

sections.name: buildEvidenceIndex
sections.title: Building the lookup once
sections.what: Goes through every case, saves its pack, and records each item under its id.
sections.why: Built once, so the pages do not rescan the data each time they draw.
sections.watch_out: A duplicate id silently overwrites the earlier item. Nothing here reports it.

sections.name: Resolution
sections.title: Result of resolving citations
sections.what: Holds the found items and the missing ids separately.
sections.why: Keeps missing citations in a list the page can show, instead of letting them disappear.

sections.name: resolve
sections.title: Looking up a citation list
sections.what: Looks up each cited id. Found items go into the resolved list and missing ids go into the dangling list.
sections.why: Stated in the header comment: a missing id must be reported, not skipped.
sections.watch_out: The results keep the order of the input list.

sections.name: AUTHORITY_TIER_LABEL
sections.title: Labels for source authority
sections.what: Gives tiers 1 to 4 a plain description of how authoritative a source is.
sections.why: The labels are copied from the Python enum, so the viewer does not invent its own names.
sections.watch_out: This table must stay in step with the enum. It has only four entries.

sections.name: authorityLabel
sections.title: Label for any tier number
sections.what: Returns the matching label, or says the tier is unmapped for any number outside the table.
sections.why: Shows an unknown tier as unknown instead of guessing a name for it.
sections.watch_out: The unmapped wording is what a reader sees when a tier is wrong, so it should stay clear.

summary: Builds a lookup from each evidence id to its item, and reports any cited id that cannot be found.
purpose: Lets a claim show the source items behind it, and makes a missing source visible instead of dropping it.
why: The header says a citation that points nowhere should be shown as a dangling citation, because that is a different statement from a claim with no evidence at all.
how: Goes through each golden case, keeps its evidence pack, and stores each item under its id. Resolving a list of ids then splits it into the items that were found and the ids that were not. Authority tiers are labelled from a fixed table.
inputs: The collected artifacts object with its cases, and a list of evidence ids to look up.
outputs: An index with a lookup by id and a list of packs by case. A resolution with the found items and the missing ids. A text label for each authority tier.
risks: If two cases reuse the same id, the later one silently replaces the earlier one. The tier labels must match the Python enum or the page will describe the wrong tier.
debug: If a citation shows as dangling, check the id in the source pack and rebuild the artifacts file. If a tier label looks wrong, compare it with the enum in packages/schema/case_input.py.
